analysis.title: Inside Commodities, November 5, 2026
key_insights: EIA week ended Oct 30: US crude stocks fell 865,000 barrels to 409.8M barrels versus a Reuters poll for a 877,000-barrel rise. Gasoline stocks fell 222,000 barrels to 209M versus a poll for a 153,000-barrel build. Distillate stocks fell 3.6M barrels to 99.3M versus an expected 100,000-barrel drop, the lowest since 2003.
US product supplied, a proxy for demand, rose 1.75M bpd to 21.96M bpd, the highest since October 2025. Refinery utilization rose 1.7 points to 94.5%. Midwest gasoline stocks hit a record low.

Brent traded at $100.25, down $3.35, and WTI at $93.01, down $3.08, on Nov 4. Crude lost as much as $4 as traders waited for Washington's next move in the Iran war after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterms.

Brent has fallen more than 14% since Monday on news that Iran's Supreme Leader gave negotiators more leeway in Qatar-mediated indirect talks. Iran then said the sides remain far apart. Oil is still about 40% above pre-war levels.

Reuters columnist Ron Bousso argues the midterm loss makes it harder for Trump to end the Iran war. He lists three options: further strikes, a quick deal, or the status quo. He says Trump keeps broad authority over military operations despite Congress.

Hormuz crude flows have recovered to about 80% of pre-war levels with US Navy-assisted convoys. The US is blockading Iranian oil exports. Two US carrier strike groups are in or near the region and a third is heading to the Gulf.

Ecuador cocoa faces El Niño risk. Analysts expect about a 10% output decline from roughly 600,000 tons produced in 2025. StoneX cut its Ecuador 2026/27 outlook by 65,000 tons (10%) to 585,000 tons. The 1997-98 El Niño cut output by more than 61%.
Mexican avocado exports to the US fell 40% during a Michoacan price dispute, with weekly shipments dropping to 11,000 tons from 28,000 tons. An agreement reached Tuesday restarts shipments Thursday.
India approved a 28.14 billion rupee ($297M) incentive policy for lithium and nickel processing to reduce reliance on China-dominated supply chains.

ArcelorMittal Q3 EBITDA was $2.02B versus an LSEG consensus of $1.96B. It booked a net loss of $391M versus a $683M profit the prior quarter, due to impairments from idling Kryvyi Rih in Ukraine. All European blast furnaces are back in operation and the full benefit of EU steel protection is expected from 2027.

Europe's gas prices are at multi-year highs, with EU storage about 75% full versus a 91% average for this time of year since 2020. Qatar LNG exports fell 65% in the first nine months of 2026. Asian LNG averaged $19.15/MMBtu in 2026 (+58% vs 2025) and the Dutch hub averaged about $18.06 (+51%).

LSEG forecasts East Asian temperatures about 3C above normal from December to March on a strong El Niño. That could free LNG supplies for Europe, which has been injecting gas faster than in 2024 and 2025.

Rabobank sees Brazil's 2026/27 soybean crop at 178M tons (down 4M from the prior season) and exports at 113M tons versus 114M tons. It expects China to buy more US soybeans following a Beijing-Washington deal.

US September refined copper imports were 194,284 tons, down 3.1% from August and nearly double September 2025's 102,279 tons. COMEX copper stocks hit a record 731,428 tons. A proposed 15% tariff on refined copper from 2027 is unconfirmed and traders hope for clarity after the midterms.

An EIB survey found 87% of EU respondents want the low-carbon shift prioritised, up from 82% in 2022. 52% favor solar, 37% wind and 19% nuclear. 55% prefer the EU to develop its own clean tech even if slower.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 EBITDA of $2.02B beat the $1.96B LSEG consensus on higher European shipments. A net loss of $391M followed Kryvyi Rih impairment charges.

sector_views.rationale: Distillate stocks are at their lowest since 2003 and demand is at a one-year high. Crude is volatile on Iran peace-talk headlines.
EU protectionism improves European pricing power while the Iran war raises energy and raw material costs.

earnings_insights: ArcelorMittal Q3 2026 EBITDA reported at $2.02B versus LSEG analyst average forecast of $1.96B (reported Nov 5). Net loss of $391M reported versus $683M profit in Q2, due to impairment and exceptional charges from idling Kryvyi Rih in Ukraine. Management expects Q4 shipments to accelerate and H2 deliveries to exceed H1.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Draw against an expected build of 877,000 barrels, supportive for crude.
Lowest since 2003, the main supply pressure point.
Draw against an expected 153,000-barrel build, with strong demand.
Up 1.7 points on the week, high refinery demand for crude.
Highest since October 2025, signalling strong fuel demand.
Down 3.1% from August but nearly double a year earlier, as metal is front-loaded ahead of a possible tariff.
Compared with a roughly 91% average for this time of year since 2020, which keeps European gas prices elevated.
Down 4M tons from the prior season, with exports seen at 113M tons.

risk_factors: Collapse of Iran peace talks or a new round of US strikes could raise crude and energy infrastructure damage risk.
A quick deal that does not address Iran's nuclear program could leave the region unstable and strain US-Gulf relations.
El Niño flooding could cut Ecuadorian cocoa output, and the strongest impact may fall in the October to January harvest.
Europe's gas market remains vulnerable to supply shocks with storage 16 points below the seasonal norm.
Unconfirmed US copper tariff timing leaves inventories and trade flows exposed.
Avocado seed weevil detections in Michoacan add to export disruption risk.
vol_and_positioning: COMEX copper stocks are at a record 731,428 tons and LME US warehouse inventories are at their highest in more than a decade, driven by front-loading ahead of a proposed 15% tariff.
geopolitical: US-Israeli war with Iran, launched Feb 28, has become a contest over control of the Strait of Hormuz since June.
Democrats won both the Senate and House in the Nov 3 midterms, in part as a rebuke over the Iran war.
Qatar is mediating indirect US-Iran talks. Iran says the sides remain far apart and wants Hormuz reopening, release of overseas funds and sanctions relief ahead of nuclear talks.
US has effectively blockaded Iran's oil exports. A third US carrier strike group is heading to the Gulf.
India's critical minerals policy targets reduced dependence on China-dominated processing and follows Chinese export controls.
Russian strikes forced the shutdown of ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih in Ukraine in September after four strikes in five weeks.
A Beijing-Washington deal is expected to lift Chinese purchases of US soybeans.
cross_bank_references: Rabobank (via Reuters): China is seen buying more US soybeans after the Beijing-Washington deal, with total Chinese soy imports stable.

tension_points.bull_case: A quick deal that fully reopens Hormuz could lower oil prices in the short term. Brent fell more than 14% in days on reports that Iran's leader gave negotiators more leeway.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran says the sides remain far apart and has little reason to agree quickly to a deal not in its favor. A deal that ignores the core nuclear issues would leave Iran stronger and risk a new confrontation. Further strikes risk more damage to energy infrastructure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Iran saying the sides remain far apart, or a resumption of US strikes, would undo the peace-deal price decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Asian temperatures forecast about 3C above normal from December to March could free LNG supplies for Europe, and EU injections are running faster than in 2024 and 2025.
tension_points.bear_case: EU storage is about 75% full versus a 91% norm, and Qatar LNG exports are down 65%. Europe's gas market remains vulnerable to global supply shocks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A colder-than-forecast winter in East Asia would increase competition for spot LNG cargoes.

theme_stances.evidence: the Middle East quagmire is likely to deepen
